facts.claim: Our Census study (ACS 2020-2024): 16,880,456 of 143,775,355 US homes, 11.74%, were built before 1940; 25.64% before 1960. Source table B25034 (Year Structure Built), fetched 2026-10-09.
State shares built before 1940: District of Columbia 31.5%, Massachusetts 30.5%, New York 30.3%.
582 counties have at least 25% of homes built before 1940; 89 counties hold half of all pre-1940 homes.

Our report engine's knob-and-tube rule: homes built through 1955; electrician evaluation $150 – $350; partial to whole-home rewire $8,000 – $30,000+; asks the inspector to confirm in writing whether any is still energized.

facts.claim: Washington home inspection standard: inspectors are not required to operate breakers or remove fuses.
facts.quote: (2) The inspector is not required to: (c) Operate circuit breakers, service disconnects or remove fuses. WAC 308-408C-110

facts.claim: Berkeley's form gives three electrician outcomes, including disconnected and not live.
facts.quote: The knob-and-tube wiring is disconnected and is not live or has been removed. Form #146

facts.claim: Washington allows insulation over knob and tube only with a written survey by a licensed electrical contractor (WAC 296-46B-394).
facts.quote: The wiring must be surveyed by an appropriately licensed electrical contractor who must certify in writing to the department that the wiring is in good condition
